title: Pulse X
label: Inspired Sounds

type.basis: Earliest-dated record in this set that sources widely call the first grime beat (FACT no. 1; SPIN; Wikipedia) and described in an interview as the first 8-bar track released. No type was designated when the name grime came into use, so the first designation is a lectotype. Oi! (promo 2001) and Venom (made 2001, released early 2002) may predate it: see the priority question.

sound.text: A single 16-bar loop: first 8 bars in a 2-step garage style, second 8 bars stripped to kick and snare; no intro, fade-out ending; a voice sample recurs every 32 bars at the switch.
Stripped down to overdriven bass bleeps and handclaps; lo-fi and minimal with large empty spaces.
Breakbeat garage deconstructed into a minimal, twisted loop.
Producer says he programmed the drum pattern in Propellerhead ReBirth, then sampled a bassline, sequencing in Digital Orchestrator.

context.text: Ranked no. 1 in FACT's 'The 20 best Grime records ever made' (credited Musical Mob, Inspired Sounds, 2002).

Widely considered the first grime beat / a 'year zero'; its minimalism is said to have set the foundations for a more MC-centred genre. Bok Bok named it his favourite example of Youngstar's 'simplistic, brutalist genius' (2014).
Ransom Note interview describes it as 'the first 8 bar track released' and says it sold out within its first week at Blackmarket (record shop); sold heavily on vinyl.
SPIN (Philip Sherburne, 2012) argues it as grime's founding track, noting Wiley's 'Eskimo' as the rival contender later in 2002.
